# Focused original/repaired/final development Std comparison

This diagnostic records three compilers on the same original standard-library inputs. The primary issue-113 comparison is **repaired baseline versus final**, with the feature option omitted. The original compiler supplies separate context for the independently reviewed prerequisite repairs. Neither a changed expected table nor a claim that reference Std is verified follows from the measurements.

| Arm | Product source |
|---|---|
| Original | `97601b75712f458de37a13bf9953a0b7825122eb` |
| Repaired baseline | `b615831aaa26fea72364627d0fe6040f10e49eee` |
| Feature compiler | `a5304cd9aeb5e4fd12700aa2e61125a904d58996` |

The repaired compiler is reconstructed from the exact public original tree plus the included audited Core patch. Composition checks the patch SHA256, changed-file scope, complete tree and Core tree against `spec.json`. It includes the separately reviewed repairs for 132, 141, 142, 143, 145, 146 and 148, and retains the existing shipped owner constant-field RHS actual type-argument substitution in the development allocation port. That one-hunk correction is shared with the final development compiler. It contains no issue-113 capability admission or operation views. Its source receipt is distinct from acceptance of every old program.

The workflow requests **14 matched jobs**: the original seven Std parts under Z3 **5.1.0** and the original development reference solver **4.16.0**. Three compiler builds and **42 verification invocations** are requested. Each part executes once per compiler; original/repaired, repaired/final and original/final comparisons reuse those three results. All three arms in a job share one host, solver executable, input checkout and current directory. Their order rotates deterministically across parts and solver axes. No integration-suite job, additional refresh axis or Unicode axis is part of this focused dispatch.

The input pin is the original development revision for all arms. Canonical helpers, workflow, expected tables, source plans and 4,608-file input receipt are retained unchanged. Before measurement, source checks validate every original input byte and regenerate the plan. The main Std project and the six sorted TargetSpecific file lists use their original project files, including the committed original `.doo` inputs. Both projects explicitly select the refresh resolver and general newtypes. The final compiler's `--extended-newtype-bases` is omitted and defaults false; the original and repaired compilers do not receive an option they lack. Every development arm omits the absent AdditionalAxioms option.

Commands preserve the canonical Std helper's four cores, verification time limit 0, project resource limits, default declaration order, explicit project settings and existing JSON logger. Same-invocation `--bprint` adds an observation of the already translated program. No seed, solver tracing, coverage, additional axiom setting or other proof option is added. The main project retains its 5,000,000 default resource limit and any original declaration-specific limits; TargetSpecific retains 1,000,000. The existing process cap is 5,400 seconds per arm, with a 240-minute job cap and at most 12 concurrent jobs. Three arms can exceed that job cap at their individual maxima; killed or absent arms remain explicitly incomplete rather than extending capacity silently.

Every arm retains its actual command/cwd, compiler version, full managed-component identity, packaged-library hashes, solver hash/version, exit, stdout/stderr, warnings, JSON declaration and batch outcomes/resource counts/seeds, and complete translated Boogie files. Normalization touches only identified compiler-version comments and known location roots in comments or diagnostic `captureState` prefixes. Formulas, declarations/order, literals, IDs, checksums, attributes, triggers and axioms stay intact. Missing, malformed or unavailable BPL/JSON is incomplete for this Std comparison, including an equal crash on two arms. These hashes cover translated Boogie **before engine VC generation**, not solver queries or passified VCs.

Each result separates the repaired/final comparison from contextual original/repaired and original/final comparisons. Original expected-table movements are reported for all three arms. The aggregate requires all seven parts on both solver axes and all three arms/context comparisons. It reports every verdict, resource/batch and normalized-BPL movement, incomplete observation and duplicate/absent part. Identical failing outcomes establish compatibility observations only. The original reference table already records an unresolved Std proof; it is not a green baseline. Std uses its original default declaration order, so resource counts can vary and source causality requires inspecting actual differences.

Source preparation and metadata checks invoke no compiler, solver or backend. Only the public workflow builds and `run.py run` verifies. Keep these exact old input plans and repaired composition fixed during attribution. A later final product requires an explicit final-pin update and fresh component receipts; it must not be substituted into results from this diagnostic.
